blurb: Sine and cosine built from power series: π, inverse branches, spherical trigonometry, Chebyshev, Fourier and Niven.

pics.alt: Partial sum of the Fourier series of a square wave, showing overshooting ripples next to each jump
pics.caption: The partial sum sin x + (1/3) sin 3x + (1/5) sin 5x + (1/7) sin 7x + (1/9) sin 9x of a square wave's Fourier series. The overshoot beside each jump never disappears as more terms are added: this is the Gibbs phenomenon.
pics.title: Gibbs phenomenon 10.svg

pics.alt: A spherical triangle with vertices u, v, w drawn on a sphere, with sides a, b, c and angles A, B, C labelled
pics.caption: A spherical triangle bounded by three great-circle arcs, with sides a, b, c and opposite angles A, B, C. The spherical law of cosines, cos c = cos a cos b + sin a sin b cos C, relates them.
pics.title: Law-of-haversines.svg
